messages:
olivia: Heads up — noticed GPUs in eu-west are stuck Pending while us-west autoscaled fine. Pods show FailedScheduling (No nodes available matching nodeSelector nvidia.com/gpu). cluster-autoscaler logs show 'no candidates' for gpu-e-* groups.
mateo: Are those nodepools mixed (spot + on-demand)? We had odd behavior when balance-similar-node-groups was off.
olivia: Yeah mixed. We had turned balance-similar-node-groups off for a cost test. Re-enabled it and CA started considering eu pools but it's still picking smaller instance types that don't fit our GPU pod resourceProfile (needs 1 gpu + 32Gi mem). Wondering about expander behavior.
chen: CA expander matters a lot with mixed types. We used --expander=most-pods for better packing of pods onto fewer nodes when GPU pods have high CPU/mem. Try --expander=most-pods or --expander=least-waste depending on what you're optimizing.
sara: Also check --max-node-provision-time — AWS spot sometimes takes >10m and CA cancels scale-ups. We set --max-node-provision-time=20m in eu-west because of spot churn.
olivia: Good call. Current CA args (from daemonset) are:
```
--expander=random
--balance-similar-node-groups=false
--scan-interval=10s
--scale-down-unneeded-time=5m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
--max-node-provision-time=10m
```
Thinking of changing to:
```
--expander=most-pods
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--max-node-provision-time=20m
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
```
mateo: I'd also bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 10m or 15m for GPU pools — we saw thrashing when small jobs land and finish quickly. And consider --nodes-min/max on GPU groups more strictly.
chen: If CA still picks wrong instance types, double-check node group auto-scaling configs in the cloud provider: labels/capacityType/schema that CA uses for filtering. For GKE/AKS we had to add resource limits annotation so CA knows GPU resource shape.
sara: Another gotcha: kube-scheduler priority/affinity. If pods have hard nodeAffinity to a zone, CA won't scale other zones. Are pods zonal? That could explain us-west vs eu-west imbalance.
olivia: Pods have zone anti-affinity to spread GPUs but we also set topologySpreadConstraints. Might be contributing. For now we'll try the expander + max-provision changes and monitor.
deploy-bot: Cluster Autoscaler (v1.23.2) rolled config update: expander=most-pods, balance-similar-node-groups=true, max-node-provision-time=20m at 2025-11-24T14:25:40Z :rocket:
mateo: After the change, watch CA logs for 'scale-up estimated' vs 'scale-up actual'. If it's estimating wrong, add --target-utilization or tweak nodeGroup sizing.
olivia: Thanks — will update after a couple of cycles. If this keeps happening we'll open a brief runbook to pin GPU workloads to dedicated on-demand pools and keep spots for stateless stuff.
